newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end steady on book squaring.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end steady on book squaring.

text.p: Australian stocks closed virtually steady on Wednesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve lifted interest rates as expected and the Easter break loomed for traders.
"It's been very bouncy...we're coming up to a long weekend, the market is closing early tomorrow so there's a lot of book squaring going on," said dealer Peter Struk of Sydney broker Reynolds & Co.
The All Ordinaries index ended up 0.9 points, or 0.04 percent, at 2,404.3.
The June Share Price Index contract ended up 16.0 points at 2,409.0, a 4.7 point premium to the physical market.
The expiring March contract, which must come into line with the physical market by close of business on Thursday, ended up 23 points at 2,404.0, a discount of just 0.3 points.
Brokers said the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to lift interest rates by 25 basis points had been widely expected, and the market would look for the timing of any further rises.
"People will now start trying to guess whether there will be one more or whether this is a oncer," said Intersuisse head of equities Andrew Sekely.

The banking sector eased slightly on the day, but dealers expected renewed interest ahead of the release of the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial sector, which is widely expected to trigger big bank takeovers.
National Australia Bank rose 15 cents to A$15.99, while Westpac Banking Corp was down seven cents at A$7.39. The ANZ Bank and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia also eased.
Others to move besides the banks included WMC Ltd, which fell nine cents to A$8.01 and topped the turnover list with almost 9.8 million shares traded.
CRA Ltd ended 17 cents stronger at A$18.47 after The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said it had bought the West Cliff mine in New South Wales from Kembla Coke and Coal, a unit of RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd.
Papua New Guinea-related stocks rose in late trading on news that Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan had announced his resignation, bringing hopes of a return to stability in the South Pacific nation.
Oil Search bounced almost ten cents to close four cents higher at A$2.57, mineral investor Orogen Minerals closed up two cents on the day at A$3.02, and Lihir was up three cents at A$2.13.
The Australian stock market will close at 1.15 p.m. (0215 GMT) on Thursday ahead of the four-day Easter break.
Brokers noted that Australian markets would be closed while New York traded on Thursday and Monday. "So not a hell of a lot is going to happen tomorrow," said one.
In other markets, the Australian dollar partially recovered overnight losses and by 4.45 p.m. (0545 GMT) was at US$0.7827 against Tuesday's close of US$0.7889.
Australian bond yields rose after the U.S. rate hike, but dealers said the market generally took the rate rise in it stride.
